["Clause 2 of the order, the direction that 'The Administrator is hereby directed to conduct such investigations as may be necessary to advise me fully within ninety days concerning the existence or development of any unfair trade practices within said Industry, utilizing the aid of the Federal Trade Commission', is a direction to a government officer. The ninety days are a report deadline, not an end, and no held record shows the investigation made or the advice given or when, so the command is neither shown exhausted nor shown to have ended on a date.", "The text does not make the direction depend on the code approval (it is framed as advice to the President about unfair trade practices in the industry, with the retained cancellation right in the approval clause as context), so the statutory repeal of the code approval and enforcement provisions is not shown to have extinguished it. Needed: a held record of the Administrator's report (which would date the exhaustion) or a reason, supported by held sources, that the direction ended with the approval.", "The approval clause of the same order (with the reserved right to cancel or modify under section 10(b)) is a plain approval that would take the repeal end."]

["Condition 1 of the order provides that 'Paragraph 3 of Section 1 of Article VIII shall not be effective until 30 days after the date this code becomes effective.' The own-terms end of that stay is 30 days after the code's effective date; the order states no effective date for the code ('to become effective in place of the Code of Labor Provisions heretofore approved'), and no held text supplies one. The end therefore cannot be dated, and cannot be assumed to fall on the repeal date.", "The same condition adds that 'A hearing shall be called as soon as practicable for the consideration and determination of the advisability of said paragraph', a direction to the Administrator with no deadline and no held record of performance. Condition 3 gives the Administrator power to disapprove acts of the code authority (code-dependent). Needed: a held record of the effective date of the Retail Food and Grocery code and of any hearing on paragraph 3 of Section 1 of Article VIII."]
